artboards.title: A round — who applied, and what became of them
Filtering, alternative — facet rail with counts

annotations.text:
Connect Marketplace — design directions

Two sides, not one: the ORGANISATIONS (supply) and the ROUNDS they answer (demand). The shipped page only had the first, which is why it read as an internal filter.

Brand values lifted from tailwind/tailwind.css: #16006d deep purple, #3843d0 indigo, #8ea1ff sky, #feaf31 marigold, #e44434 sunset, 10px radii, Work Sans.

All aggregate figures are the real ones now on prod. Organisation names are invented; the round names, counts and dates are real.

Two filtering directions, same data.

LEFT — segments as the primary control. One click gets the segment you actually work ('on the bench', 'no contact on file'), each carrying its count and a sentence saying why it matters. Refiners stay secondary.

RIGHT — a facet rail. Every value shows its count BEFORE you click, and filters combine. Better for exploring; heavier chrome, and a second column of screen.

The round page is what makes this a marketplace rather than a list.

It answers: who applied, what became of them, and what was asked. The 'since this round' column is the payoff of joining EOI history to pulse delivery — you can see which applicants from a 2025 round actually went on to deliver.

An open round shows the same page with a live applicant count and a deadline.
